ashley (Docs): Quick announcement: we're releasing Python SDK v2.0.0-rc1 to PyPI and publishing a docs refresh focused on async-first usage. This RC introduces an async client, renamed APIs, and a migration path from the legacy sync client. RC period is 2 weeks before GA. Please scan migration notes and call out any missing edge-case examples.

samir (SDK): TL;DR changelog: async-first Client (redwood.async_sdk.AsyncClient), generate() -> text_generate(), streaming via async iterators, improved batching defaults, and a default model swap optimized for latency. Breaking change: sync.Client is deprecated and slated for removal in v3.0 (~6 months).

samir (SDK): Migration snippet:
```python
# legacy sync usage
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="${API_KEY}")
resp = c.generate('Compose a short mission statement')
print(resp.text)

# new async usage
from redwood.async_sdk import AsyncClient
c = AsyncClient(api_key="${API_KEY}")
resp = await c.text_generate('Compose a short mission statement')
async for chunk in resp.stream():
    print(chunk.text)
```

samir (SDK): We're releasing a short-lived compat shim package (redwood-compat) to ease large codebase rollouts, but recommend migrating to async to benefit from continuous batching and KV caching.

docs-bot: Published: https://docs.redwood.inference/sdk/python/async-migration 1 examples, API diff, FAQ, and a deprecation timeline included.

maria (Eng): Quick perf question: do low-concurrency single-request clients see any regression?

samir (SDK): In our internal benchmarks, async shows ~10-20% p95 latency improvements for multi-request workloads due to continuous batching. For single-request low-concurrency flows, latency should be comparable; note that the default model selection change can shift medians slightly. We'll call this out in the FAQ.

ashley (Docs): I'll add the deprecation timeline to the SDK landing page, link the shim, and include an explicit rollback plan for customers who hit issues. Marking this as high-priority for the next docs sprint.
